name: Which cabinet finishes work best in humid bathrooms?

mainEntity.name: What finishes and materials are most resistant to steam, moisture, and daily wipe-downs in bathroom vanities?
mainEntity.text: What finishes and materials are most resistant to steam, moisture, and daily wipe-downs in bathroom vanities?

acceptedAnswer.text: Bathroom vanities face a different challenge than kitchen cabinets because steam and splash exposure are constant. The best-performing systems usually combine moisture-resistant substrate selection with a durable finish that fully seals all sides, edges, and cutouts. Proper edge sealing is just as important as the color coat, because water often enters through seams and unprotected corners. Painted MDF is common for smooth vanity fronts, but it must be sealed correctly to avoid swelling. Solid wood can also work, but it moves more with humidity changes. Ask whether the finish is designed for bathroom use, how the sink cutout is protected, and whether interior surfaces receive the same level of sealing as the exterior. Ventilation matters too. Even a great finish can fail early if the room traps steam and condensation. For luxury bathrooms, durability should be specified before style is finalized.
acceptedAnswer.description: Bathroom cabinetry should use moisture-resistant materials and a finish that seals edges well, such as catalyzed paint, conversion varnish, or quality lacquer systems. MDF can work for painted vanities if it is properly sealed, but edge protection is critical. Poorly sealed wood or low-grade coatings are more likely to swell, peel, or discolor.
